question.text: The equilibrium constants $K_{P_1}$ and $K_{P_2}$ for the reactions $X \rightleftharpoons 2 Y$ and $Z \rightleftharpoons P+Q$, respectively are in the ratio of $1: 9$. If the degree of dissociation of $X$ and $Z$ be equal then the ratio of total pressure at these equilibria is

solution.text:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& X \rightleftharpoons 2 Y \\
& 10 \\
& (1-x) \quad 2 x \\
& k_{p_1}=\frac{(2 x)^2}{(1-x)}\left(\frac{P_1}{1+x}\right)^1 \\
& Z \rightleftharpoons P+Q \\
& 100 \\
& (1-x) \quad x \quad x \\
& \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{p}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{x}^2}{(1-\mathrm{x})}\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_2}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right)^1 \\
& \frac{4 \times \mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2}=\frac{1}{9} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2}=\frac{1}{36} \\
&
\end{aligned}
$$
